name: Coinchenn

attributes.attribute: warrior woman under a death curse against her daughter's marriage
daughter whose wedding would bring the death of Coinchenn
king of Tara who won Delbcháem with fairy help

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Coinchenn was a warrior woman under a death curse in an Irish tale. The curse would kill her if her daughter Delbcháem ever married. Coinchenn took on every suitor who came for the maidens hand. She beat most of them and set their heads on poles around her house to make a fence. She hid her daughter in a high tower. One man was her match, and even he needed fairy help to win. That man was Art Mac Cuinn, king of Tara, and he won Delbcháem in the end.

okr.objective: Coinchenn guards her daughter against suitors until the king of Tara wins her.
